title: Career Counselor (MGySgt to Sgt) PMOS, DC M&RA
raw_text:
1.     MOS 4821, Career Counselor (MGySgt to Sgt) PMOS, DC M&RA

    a. Summary. The Career Counselor serves as the commander's primary
advisor for enlisted retention matters and is crucial in guiding and
assisting enlisted personnel in their career development across Marine Corps
enlisted components. The Career Counselor must be thoroughly knowledgeable
of the reenlistment process, to include prospecting, reenlistment ceremonies,
career information programs, and associated policies. They further provide
valuable guidance and support to service members. This MOS will be assigned
and voided only by the authority of the CMC (MM).

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must possess a GT score of 100 or higher.

             (2) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in reference (bj).

             (3) Security requirement:

                 (a) Secret security clearance eligibility.

            (b) Marines conducting lateral moves to the 4821 MOS must possess
secret clearance eligibility.

            (c) Marines who are reenlisting must possess an adjudicated
secret security clearance or favorably adjudicated national agency check/
local agency check prior finalizing their reenlistment.

       c.    Requirements

             (1) Complete Basic Career Planner Course (M0881D6), MCRD San Diego,
CA.

        (2) Failure to attend and complete the PMOS training may result in an
PMOS reclassification or separation per current MMEA and RA guidelines and
applicable MCOs.

        (3) Advanced Career Planner Course (M08KZ91) is designed for Career
Planners who currently are or will be taking on the functions and duties of a
Career Planner SNCOIC. Once a Career Planner has obtained the rank of staff
sergeant, they are required to attend the Advance Career Planning Course
(ACPC) within 2 years or prior to assignment to a career planner SNCOIC
billet, whichever is less.

       d.    Duties

        (1) Coordinate with the commander and sergeant major on developing,
coordinating, and implementing retention campaign plans that provide
education on retention, career progression, and development programs focused
on meeting retention goals.

        (2) Provide executive guidance and counseling regarding career
opportunities, promotions, special duty assignments, and professional
development.




                                         3-308                        Enclosure (1)
 3133                                                           NAVMC 1200.1L



        (3) Provide fundamental manpower professional military education and
briefings to Marine Corps units concerning career progression/development
programs.

        (4) Schedule and conduct interviews with service members, providing
individual career counseling to assist in sound career decision-making.

        (5) Assist service members in exploring and evaluating their
education, training, interests, and capabilities to set goals and make
informed career decisions.

        (6) Conduct preliminary screening and administrative processing,
ensuring accurate and efficient completion of necessary documents such as
reenlistment, lateral move, and extension forms.

        (7) Maintain records related to reenlistment, lateral moves, special
duty assignments, reserve contracts, prior service enlisted program/
continuous reenlistments, selective retention bonus program, and career
counseling, ensuring accuracy and compliance with regulations.

        (8) Collect and examine retention and attrition data, conducting
trend analysis to identify areas for improvement and develop targeted
strategies.

        (9) Identify job skills and training opportunities that enhance and
boost service members' job satisfaction. Coordinate required tests,
interviews, and physicals for lateral move candidates.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Employment, Recruitment, and Placement Specialists 13-1071.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Recruiter, 8411.




                                         3-309                   Enclosure (1)
 3134                                                                 NAVMC 1200.1L

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
